blurb: Indy, NASCAR and Formula 1: legends, firsts and traditions

questions.q: What does the Indianapolis 500 winner traditionally drink right after the race?
questions.fact: Louis Meyer started it in 1936, sipping buttermilk after his third Indy 500 win.
questions.src: nbcwashington.com 'Why does the Indy 500 winner drink milk?' (Louis Meyer, 1936, buttermilk, his third win)

questions.q: Indy's start/finish line keeps a strip of the track's original 1909 bricks. How wide is it?
questions.fact: Dale Jarrett and crew chief Todd Parrott started the kiss-the-bricks tradition after the 1996 Brickyard 400.
questions.src: cms.ims.com Yard of Bricks page (36-inch strip of original bricks laid fall 1909; Dale Jarrett and crew chief Todd Parrott kissed the bricks after the 1996 Brickyard 400)

questions.q: In 2017, which Formula 1 champion skipped the Monaco Grand Prix to race in the Indy 500?
questions.fact: Alonso led 27 laps before his engine failed 21 laps from the end, and he was voted the race's Rookie of the Year.
questions.src: Wikipedia '2017 Indianapolis 500' (skipped Monaco; led 27 laps; engine failure lap 179 of 200; voted Rookie of the Year)

questions.q: In 1977, who became the first driver to win the Indianapolis 500 four times?
questions.fact: Al Unser (1987), Rick Mears (1991) and Helio Castroneves (2021) later joined him as four-time winners.
questions.src: indycar.com 2021-07-21 four-time winners story (Foyt first in 1977; Al Unser 1987, Mears 1991, Castroneves 2021). Bobby Unser won three

questions.q: Which NASCAR legend is known simply as The King?
questions.fact: Petty won 200 Cup Series races and seven championships.
questions.src: nascarhall.com 'Petty's prime years' (calls him The King; 200 Cup wins, 7 titles); Britannica Richard Petty (200 wins, 7 titles)

questions.q: Which NASCAR race is nicknamed The Great American Race?
questions.fact: The winner's trophy honors GM designer Harley Earl and is topped by a model of his Firebird I concept car.
questions.src: Nickname textbook; Wikipedia 'Harley J. Earl Trophy' (GM designer, NASCAR's 2nd commissioner; Firebird I model on top; awarded since 1959)

questions.q: Starting in 2006, Jimmie Johnson won how many NASCAR Cup championships in a row?
questions.fact: His seventh title, in 2016, matched the totals of Richard Petty and Dale Earnhardt.
questions.src: Britannica Jimmie Johnson (five straight titles 2006-2010, record-tying seven); Petty and Earnhardt seven each per nascarhall.com/textbook

questions.q: Who won the first Daytona 500, in 1959, in a finish so close it took three days to decide?
questions.fact: Lee, Richard Petty's father, edged Johnny Beauchamp, who was first named the winner.
questions.src: history.com This Day in History Feb 22 (Lee Petty beat Johnny Beauchamp in a photo finish; Beauchamp first named winner; Petty named champ three days later)

questions.q: Which Formula 1 team is famous for its red cars and prancing horse badge?
questions.fact: The badge's yellow background is the color of Modena, Enzo Ferrari's hometown.
questions.src: Wikipedia 'Prancing Horse' (canary yellow is the colour of Modena, Enzo Ferrari's hometown)

questions.q: Which Netflix docuseries, first released in 2019, goes behind the scenes of Formula 1?
questions.fact: Its first season followed the 2018 F1 season and arrived on Netflix on March 8, 2019.
questions.src: Wikipedia 'Formula 1: Drive to Survive season 1' (released 8 March 2019, documents 2018 season). Distractors are 2023 Netflix golf/tennis/NFL docuseries

questions.q: Which American won the 1978 Formula 1 world championship?
questions.fact: Andretti also won the 1967 Daytona 500 and the 1969 Indianapolis 500.
questions.src: guinnessworldrecords.com first driver to win Indy 500, Daytona 500 and F1 title (Daytona 1967, Indy 1969, F1 1978). Phil Hill's title was 1961

questions.q: Lewis Hamilton won his first F1 world title in 2008 driving for which team?
questions.fact: At 23 he was then F1's youngest champion; Sebastian Vettel broke that mark in 2010.
questions.src: formula1.com 'The youngest world champions' (Hamilton 23y300d in 2008, youngest at the time; Vettel 23y133d, 2010 Abu Dhabi). McLaren 2008 textbook

blurb: Sports on film and TV, from The Bad News Bears to Ted Lasso

questions.q: The 1993 film Rudy follows a walk-on who dreams of playing football for which school?
questions.fact: Sean Astin starred, and it was the first film Notre Dame let shoot on campus since Knute Rockne, All American.
questions.src: Wikipedia 'Rudy (film)' (1993; Sean Astin; first film Notre Dame allowed on campus since Knute Rockne, All American)

questions.q: Remember the Titans (2000) tells the story of a 1971 high school football team from which state?
questions.fact: Denzel Washington played coach Herman Boone, and the real 1971 Titans won the state title.
questions.src: Wikipedia 'Herman Boone' (T.C. Williams HS, Alexandria, Virginia; 1971 Titans 13-0 state champions; Denzel Washington played him)

questions.q: Ford v Ferrari (2019) recreates Ford's battle to win which race in 1966?
questions.fact: In the UK it was titled Le Mans '66, and Christian Bale played driver Ken Miles.
questions.src: topgear.com first look at 'Le Mans '66' (UK title; Bale as Ken Miles, Damon as Shelby; 1966 24 Hours of Le Mans)

questions.q: Hoosiers (1986) was inspired by which small Indiana school's 1954 state basketball title?
questions.fact: Bobby Plump's shot with seconds left beat Muncie Central, a school about ten times Milan's size, 32-30.
questions.src: Indiana Historical Bureau marker 'Milan Miracle' (in.gov): 32-30 over Muncie Central, about ten times Milan's size, Plump's winning shot, inspired Hoosiers (1986)

questions.q: In Happy Gilmore (1996), Adam Sandler plays a failed hockey player who finds success in which sport?
questions.fact: Carl Weathers, Apollo Creed in the Rocky films, played Happy's golf mentor, Chubbs Peterson.
questions.src: Wikipedia 'Happy Gilmore' (Feb 1996; hockey to golf; Carl Weathers as Chubbs Peterson). Weathers as Apollo Creed textbook. Replaced Space Jam (repeats B6 draft's Space Jam/Michael Jordan question)

questions.q: Field of Dreams (1989), starring Kevin Costner, is set on a farm in which state?
questions.fact: In 2021, MLB played a real game next to the movie field, and the White Sox beat the Yankees 9-8.
questions.src: thescore.com Aug 2021 (White Sox 9, Yankees 8 in Dyersville, Iowa, park built beside the 1989 film's site); Iowa setting textbook

questions.q: Which actor starred as boxer Adonis Creed in the 2015 film Creed?
questions.fact: Sylvester Stallone was Oscar-nominated for playing Rocky in both Rocky (1976) and Creed.
questions.src: smithsonianmag.com 2016 'Stallone joins Oscars elite team of actors nominated twice for same role' (Rocky 1976 and Creed); Michael B. Jordan as Adonis Creed textbook

questions.q: Who played the grumpy Little League coach in The Bad News Bears (1976)?
questions.fact: Tatum O'Neal played star pitcher Amanda, two years after winning an Oscar at age 10.
questions.src: Wikipedia 'The Bad News Bears' (Matthau as coach Morris Buttermaker; O'Neal as star pitcher Amanda; released April 7, 1976); guinnessworldrecords.com (O'Neal won Paper Moon Oscar 2 April 1974 aged 10)

questions.q: In Ted Lasso, an American football coach is hired to manage an English team in which sport?
questions.fact: Jason Sudeikis first played Ted Lasso in 2013 NBC Sports ads for its Premier League coverage.
questions.src: si.com 2020 'Ted Lasso and the journey from viral promo' (2013 NBC Sports promo for its Premier League rights; team is AFC Richmond)

questions.q: TV's Friday Night Lights (2006-2011) followed a high school football team in which state?
questions.fact: It grew from H.G. Bissinger's 1990 book about Permian High School in Odessa, Texas.
questions.src: Wikipedia 'Friday Night Lights: A Town, a Team, and a Dream' (Bissinger, 1990, Permian HS, Odessa, Texas; TV series 2006-2011)

questions.q: Monday Night Football debuted in 1970 on which TV network?
questions.fact: Keith Jackson, Howard Cosell and Don Meredith called that first game, Browns vs. Jets.
questions.src: deseret.com 2024 'Monday Night Football debuted in 1970' (Sept 21, 1970, ABC, Browns 31 Jets 21, Jackson/Cosell/Meredith)

questions.q: The sitcom Coach (1989-97) starred Craig T. Nelson as a college football coach in which state?
questions.fact: Hayden Fox coached the fictional Minnesota State Screaming Eagles, then a pro expansion team, the Orlando Breakers.
questions.src: Wikipedia 'Coach (TV series)' (ABC 1989-97; Minnesota State University Screaming Eagles, about an hour from the Twin Cities; final two seasons Orlando Breakers expansion team)

blurb: How teams got their names, mascots and logos, pro and college

questions.q: The Baltimore Ravens took their name from a famous poem by which writer?
questions.fact: In a 1996 Baltimore Sun phone poll, Ravens won 22,463 of 33,748 votes, beating Americans and Marauders.
questions.src: baltimoreravens.com 'Naming the team' (Sun 'Sundial' poll March 1996; 33,748 callers, Ravens 22,463; finalists Americans, Marauders; Poe's poem)

questions.q: The Toronto Raptors' 1994 name was inspired by the dinosaurs of which hit movie?
questions.fact: Raptors won a 1994 fan vote over finalists that included Bobcats, Dragons and Grizzlies.
questions.src: museumoftoronto.com 'The Raptors were almost named the Bobcats' (1994 call-in contest; Jurassic Park dinosaur craze; finalists Grizzlies, Bobcats, Dragons, Hogs)

questions.q: The NBA's Utah Jazz kept the name they first used in which city?
questions.fact: After the 1979 move to Salt Lake City, a contest sought a new nickname, but the Jazz name stayed.
questions.src: historytogo.utah.gov 'Utah Jazz' (New Orleans Jazz expansion 1974; moved for 1979-80; kept name despite a contest for a new one)

questions.q: The Dodgers' name traces to 1890s Brooklyn, where pedestrians had to dodge what?
questions.fact: Before Dodgers stuck, the Brooklyn club was also called the Bridegrooms, the Superbas and the Robins.
questions.src: news.sportslogos.net 'How the Dodgers finally got their name' (Trolley Dodgers from 1890s electric streetcars; Bridegrooms 1888, Superbas 1899, Robins 1914). Old fact said 'first nicknamed', which was wrong

questions.q: Which NHL team introduced Gritty, its googly-eyed orange mascot, in 2018?
questions.fact: Gritty was the Flyers' first mascot since 1976, and he became an internet star almost overnight.
questions.src: si.com 2018-09-24 'Flyers unveil new mascot Gritty' (unveiled Sept 24, 2018; team's first mascot since 1976)

questions.q: Uga, a line of live white English bulldogs, is the mascot of which school?
questions.fact: Uga V made the cover of Sports Illustrated in April 1997.
questions.src: georgiadogs.com 'History of Our Mascot' (white English bulldog line from Uga I in 1956, Seiler family of Savannah; Uga V on SI cover April 28, 1997). Yale, Miss. State, Butler bulldogs have other names

questions.q: The University of Oregon's Duck mascot is modeled on which famous cartoon duck?
questions.fact: Athletic director Leo Harris and Walt Disney agreed on it with a 1947 handshake; a written contract followed in 1973.
questions.src: University of Oregon Libraries SCUA blog 'The Oregon Mascot, Part 2' (1947 Harris-Disney handshake deal; formal contract 1973)

questions.q: The San Diego Chicken, a famous 1970s mascot, was first hired to promote what?
questions.fact: Ted Giannoulas debuted the suit in 1974, handing out Easter eggs at the San Diego Zoo for radio station KGB.
questions.src: Wikipedia 'San Diego Chicken' (Ted Giannoulas; 1974 KGB-FM promotion handing out Easter eggs at the San Diego Zoo)

questions.q: Which NFL team's helmets feature a single blue star?
questions.fact: Texas is nicknamed the Lone Star State, and the Cowboys began play in 1960.
questions.src: Textbook (Cowboys' blue star helmet; Texas the Lone Star State; Cowboys began play 1960)

questions.q: Which NHL team's logo is a winged wheel, a fitting symbol for the Motor City?
questions.fact: The team was called the Cougars, then the Falcons, before becoming the Red Wings in 1932.
questions.src: detroithistorical.org Encyclopedia of Detroit 'Detroit Red Wings' (Cougars from 1926, Falcons 1930-31, Red Wings in 1932)

questions.q: The Golden State Warriors' logo, introduced in 2010, shows which bridge?
questions.fact: The Bay Bridge links San Francisco and Oakland, the Warriors' home city when the logo debuted.
questions.src: Wikipedia 'Golden State Warriors' (2010 logo shows the new eastern span of the San Francisco-Oakland Bay Bridge); secureyourtrademark.com logo history (Bay Bridge replaced Golden Gate)

questions.q: The Hartford Whalers' famous logo hides which letter in the space between a W and a whale tail?
questions.fact: The Whalers moved to North Carolina in 1997 and became the Carolina Hurricanes.
questions.src: ctpublic.org 2023 Peter Good obituary (logo combines whale tail, W and a negative-space H; team moved to North Carolina in 1997). Hurricanes name textbook

blurb: Hawks, M's, Zags, Cougs, Dawgs and more: Washington's teams

questions.q: Which Mariners superstar was nicknamed The Kid?
questions.fact: He entered the Hall of Fame in 2016 with 99.3 percent of the vote, a record at the time.
questions.src: baseballhall.org 'Griffey Jr. and Piazza elected' (437 of 440, 99.32%, record at the time, topping Seaver's 98.84%); 'The Kid' textbook

questions.q: Storm star Lauren Jackson, the WNBA's No. 1 draft pick in 2001, is from which country?
questions.fact: Jackson won the WNBA MVP award three times, in 2003, 2007 and 2010.
questions.src: wnba.com 'Lauren Jackson by the numbers' (No. 1 pick 2001 by Seattle; Australian; MVP 2003, 2007, 2010)

questions.q: Which future NBA star played college basketball at Washington State from 2008 to 2011?
questions.fact: His father, Mychal Thompson, was the No. 1 pick in the 1978 NBA Draft.
questions.src: wsucougars.com 2011 draft story (three years at WSU, 2010-11 junior year; father Mychal Thompson No. 1 pick 1978 by Portland). Thomas and Roy played at UW, Lillard at Weber State

questions.q: Which Seahawks defensive tackle was named NFL Defensive Player of the Year in 1992, when Seattle went 2-14?
questions.fact: Kennedy played all 11 of his NFL seasons in Seattle and entered the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2012.
questions.src: profootballhof.com Cortez Kennedy (DT, 1992 Defensive Player of the Year on a 2-14 team; all 11 seasons 1990-2000 with Seattle; class of 2012). Replaced Steve Largent (later a U.S. congressman: DECK_SPEC rule 4, no politicians after 1950)

questions.q: Marshawn Lynch's famous 2011 playoff touchdown run against New Orleans is nicknamed the Beast what?
questions.fact: Fans celebrated so wildly that a seismic station near the stadium recorded the shaking.
questions.src: pnsn.org blog 'Marshawn Lynch shakes the PNSN' (Jan 8, 2011, 67-yard TD vs Saints; recorded at station KDK on Occidental Ave)

questions.q: Edgar Martinez's series-winning 1995 playoff hit, known as The Double, beat which team?
questions.fact: Ken Griffey Jr. raced all the way home from first base with the winning run in the 11th inning.
questions.src: SABR Games Project Oct 8, 1995 (Mariners 6, Yankees 5 in 11, ALDS Game 5; Cora tied it, Griffey scored the winner from first)

questions.q: Jalen Suggs' overtime buzzer-beater sent Gonzaga to the 2021 title game past which team?
questions.fact: His banked 3-pointer from about 40 feet won it 93-90 and kept Gonzaga unbeaten at 31-0.
questions.src: abc7.com April 2021 (Gonzaga 93, UCLA 90 OT, Final Four; banked 3 from about 40 feet; 31-0; Baylor next in the final)

questions.q: Washington's 12-0 Huskies split the 1991 national title with which team?
questions.fact: Don James's Huskies beat Michigan in the Rose Bowl; the coaches' poll picked UW, and the AP picked Miami.
questions.src: UW Magazine 'The champs wore roses' (12-0; Rose Bowl 34-14 over Michigan; USA Today/CNN coaches' poll No. 1 UW, AP No. 1 Miami; Don James)

questions.q: What is the name of the football rivalry game between UW and Washington State?
questions.fact: The schools first played in 1900 in Seattle, and the game ended in a 5-5 tie.
questions.src: Wikipedia 'Apple Cup' (first game Nov 29, 1900, Seattle, 5-5 tie). Draft fact's 'name since 1962' dropped: Wikipedia says trophy first awarded 1963

questions.q: The SuperSonics' name was inspired by which company's planned supersonic jetliner?
questions.fact: Fans picked the name in 1967, just after Boeing won the SST contract. The jet was canceled in 1971 and never flew.
questions.src: Museum of Flight blog 'Seattle's Supersonic Legacy' (name chosen Feb 1967; Boeing beat Lockheed for the contract end of Dec 1966; canceled spring 1971; no prototype flew)

questions.q: When the Kraken began play in 2021, how many teams did the NHL have?
questions.fact: Their home, Climate Pledge Arena, was built under the old KeyArena's landmark roof.
questions.src: lex18.com/AP 2021 'Seattle Kraken officially become NHL's 32nd franchise'; constructiondive.com (arena kept KeyArena's 1962 roof, dug down beneath it)

questions.q: Seattle's first Sounders club began play in 1974 in which league?
questions.fact: Those Sounders lost the 1977 Soccer Bowl to the New York Cosmos in Pele's last competitive game.
questions.src: historylink.org 'Original Seattle Sounders (1974-1983)' (NASL; lost 1977 Soccer Bowl 2-1 to Cosmos); pdxmonthly.com 2017 (Soccer Bowl '77 in Portland was Pele's final competitive match)
